Lilly Q3 2026 earnings beat, guidance raised

8.text: Eli Lilly beat Q3 2026 earnings and revenue estimates, with revenue up 39% to $24.4 billion on Mounjaro and Zepbound strength, and raised guidance. Shares rose about 4% premarket and hit a 52-week high, though pricing pressure and competition remain concerns.

6.text: Healthcare ETF comparisons show Eli Lilly’s GLP-1 drugs drove iShares’ IHE to 38.2% returns, beating VanEck’s PPH. Other articles cover Merck, Pfizer, Bristol Myers Squibb, Johnson & Johnson, and healthcare funds, with no new Eli Lilly developments.

5.text: Lilly reported Phase 1 data showing its FRα-targeting ADC sofetabart mipitecan plus bevacizumab achieved a 79% response rate and 100% disease control in platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer, and first-line olomorasib data in KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC. It also reported Phase 3 TRANSCEND-T2D-2 results showing retatrutide beat Ozempic on A1C reduction and weight loss, licensed the ADDF's SpeechDx dataset, and plans to merge its U.S. and international divisions.

9.text: Eli Lilly's retatrutide beat Novo's Ozempic in a head-to-head Phase III diabetes trial, delivering roughly double the weight loss (44-47 lbs vs. 21 lbs over 80 weeks) with higher side-effect rates. A federal judge also rejected Novo's bid to block Lilly's obesity drug ads, finding no meaningful sales harm.

12.text: Tech earnings from Microsoft, Google, Amazon, ServiceNow and Fortinet drove sharp Nasdaq swings, with Google and Fortinet diving while Microsoft rose; the Fed held rates steady and the S&P 500 gained a third session. Eli Lilly is not mentioned in these articles.

7.text: A survey finds more Americans now use GLP-1 drugs for weight loss than for diabetes, with users cutting sweets and changing clothing sizes. This signals a growing market for Eli Lilly's obesity treatments.
